2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

When the said bus was near Mogili Ghat, Bangarupalem Mandalam, on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road, Chittoor District, Andhrapradesh, at that time one Tata Goods carriage container lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777, came from the opposite direction i.e.

sentences.text: Due to said impact, the said bus got dashed to another lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE-7619, which was behind the bus.
As a result of which, the driver of said bus died on the spot and the passengers in the said bus sustained grievous injuries.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as APSRTC bus driver at Alipiri Depot, Tirupathi Urban, Andhra Pradesh and was getting monthly salary of Rs.58,228/-.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

The Bangarupalem Urban Police have registered the case against the driver of the said container lorry for the offences punishable under Section 106(1),
125(a) and 281 of Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per anum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, three vehicles are involved in the alleged accident, but the petitioner has not made the owners and insurers of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 as parties to the present petition.
The respective owners and insurers of the said vehicles are necessary parties to the claim petition and the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Further it is contended that, the petition is filed beyond the limitation period and no proper, cogent reasons have been assigned to condone the delay in filing the claim petition.
Hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.

Further it is contended that,
the alleged accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the drivers of all the three vehicles.
If the drivers of all the three vehicles were careful and vigilant, they could have avoided the accident.
The contributory negligence is more on the part of drivers of APSRTC bus and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619.
Unauthorized passengers were traveling in lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 and to get compensation to them a false case has been filed only against the driver of lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.
If any compensation is to be paid, it is to be paid by the owners and insurers of APSRTC bus and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the liability of this respondent if any is subject to terms and conditions and limitations of insurance policy and provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, if policy is issued in favour of the owner of container lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB- 7777 was driving the same without possessing a valid and effective driving licence, fitness certificate and permit.
Hence, there is a violation of policy conditions, rules and regulations of Motor Vehicle Act.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation and not liable to indemnify the owner of the said vehicle.

But, it has failed to establish the said contentions.
The respondent No.2 has neither adduced any evidence, nor produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even it has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777 and dashing the same to the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03- Z-5419 of the deceased, proceeding on the other lane in the opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased/driver of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 or driver of lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 or there was any contributory negligence on their part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of the road, on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road, at Mogili Ghat,
Bangarupalem Mandal, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, in between the offending lorry bearing No.AP-15- TB-7777 and APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7619,
proceeding on the other lane of National highway road in the opposite direction.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.7 Motor Vehicle Accident report, the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the drivers of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB- 7619, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that,
the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

14. Further, the Ex.P.6 Post-mortem report clearly speaks that, the deceased S. Manogaran has died due to injury to brain and long bones leading to hypovolemic shock sustained in the road traffic accident.

sentences.text: Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.

21. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, they are legal representatives of the deceased S.
Manogaran and they were depending on him.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
22. Age and income of the deceased:
The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 55 years.
To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased S. Manogaran, which is marked as Ex.P.13, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 23-09-1968.
The accident has taken place on 13-09-2024.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 56 years.

The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as APSRTC bus driver at Alipiri Depot, Tirupathi Urban, Andhra Pradesh and was getting monthly salary of Rs.58,228/-.

To substantiate the same, they have produced the Employee Identity card, driving licence of deceased, salary slip of deceased for the month of June to August-2024 and bank account statement of deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.17 to 20.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the deceased was working as driver in APSRTC, Andhra Pradesh.
Further, as per the Ex.P.19 salary slips, in the month of August-2024 the gross salary of the deceased was Rs.55,742/- per month, which was his last drawn salary.
After deducting professional tax of Rs.200/-, the net salary of the deceased will be Rs.55,542/- per month.

Therefore, the income of the deceased, as on the date of accident, is held at Usha Rani M vs Sudhakar Babu G on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111577628/

Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.

Further, the insurance policy bearing No.3379/04006662/000/00, issued by the respondent No.2,
in respect of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777, was valid from 02-08-2024 to 01-08-2025.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 13-09-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777, the accident has occurred and the deceased S. Manogaran has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.47,78,883/- from the respondent No.2, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.47,78,883/- (Rupees forty seven lakh seventy eight thousand eight hundred and eighty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES
1 . Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased S. Manogaran S/o A.N. Sampath has succumbed to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident, alleged to have been occurred on 13- 09-2024 at about 3.10 p.m., on Mogili Ghat, Bangarupalem, Chittoor- Palamaner NH-69 road, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA Goods Carriage Container Lorry bearing registration No.AP-15-TB-7777 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3 . What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.
Whereas, the respondent No.2/insurer of offending vehicle has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased/driver of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and driver of lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE- 7619 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777.
When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the drivers of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB- 7619, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that,
the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.12 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.AP-15-TB- 7777 and the deceased Manogaran has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15- TB-7777 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Manogaran in the said accident and cause of his death.
14. Further, the Ex.P.6 Post-mortem report clearly speaks that, the deceased S. Manogaran has died due to injury to brain and long bones leading to hypovolemic shock sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is absolutely no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
17.
20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.
In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, they are legal representatives of the deceased S.
Manogaran and they were depending on him.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
